requirement: Connect dispatch planning and execution through the public dispatch entry.
finding: index.mjs re-exports normalize, queue, capacity, access, schedule, retry, serialize, storage, manifest, publisher and telemetry but not executor.mjs or runtime.mjs, so the execution operations defined in executor.mjs (for example executeAuthorizedPlan, runEligibleStops and pendingStops) are not reachable through the public dispatch entry.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `nextRetryDelay` applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided `retryAfter`.
finding: nextRetryDelay (retry.mjs:24) tests retryAfter for truthiness, so a finite numeric retryAfter of 0 is ignored and computeBackoff applies instead of the server delay. A direct check of nextRetryDelay(1, 0) returned 500 instead of 0. Rules 6 and 7 (dispatch-policy.md:15-16) require a finite numeric retryAfter to replace the computed backoff.

requirement: `executeAuthorizedPlan` rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: Line 4 evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) as an argument before unlessForbidden checks canPlanRoute, so dispatch runs before the authorization decision. A direct check with an unauthorized actor invoked dispatch once.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `stopsForDriver` returns exactly the stops whose assigned driver is the given driver.
finding: stopsForDriver compares stop.driver directly (queue.mjs:30) and ignores the reassignment driver. Rule 30 (dispatch-policy.md:63) defines the assigned driver as the reassignment driver when a reassignment exists. A direct check with a stop reassigned to D2 returned no stops for D2.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `writePlanAtomically` renames the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `chooseDeparture` applies every Departure timing rule.
finding: chooseDeparture moves a departure inside the blackout (hour 3) to the blackout end hour 5 (schedule.mjs:6, with atUtcHour at line 20). Hour 5 is outside the departure window that ends at hour 4 (schedule.mjs:1). Rule 14 (dispatch-policy.md:26) requires such a departure to be refused, but a direct check at 2026-10-25T03:00:00Z returned a non-null departure.

requirement: `redactNestedDriverToken` removes a nested driver token from telemetry.
`emitPlanCreated` emits `plan.created` only after storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated hands its emitter callback to savePlan as onStored, and savePlan passes it to store.write as onCommit (storage.mjs:4). docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md does not define store.write or when onCommit runs relative to a durable write, so whether plan.created is emitted only after storage succeeds cannot be established from the staged bytes and the governing contracts.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `hasDuplicateRouteKeys` reports duplicates exactly when two stops are duplicates.
finding: The identity key on line 18 concatenates depotId and the normalized routeKey with no separator. Depot 'A1' with route key 'B' and depot 'A' with route key '1B' both produce 'A1B', so hasDuplicateRouteKeys reports a duplicate for stops that are not duplicates; a direct check returned true. Rule 19 (dispatch-policy.md:37) defines the identity as the depotId together with the normalized route key.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `parseRetryCount` accepts exactly the valid retry counts and otherwise returns a result whose `ok` is `false`.
finding: Line 4 relies on Number(value) coercion, so the empty string (Number('') is 0) and '1e0' are accepted; direct checks returned ok true for both. Rule 22 (dispatch-policy.md:43) accepts text retry counts only when they are one or more base-10 digits.

requirement: `remainingVehicleCapacity` never returns a negative value.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `pendingStops` returns every stop except the delivered stops.
finding: pendingStops excludes only state 'delivered' (line 19), so a stop with state 'handedOver' is returned as pending; a direct check returned 1 pending stop for that input. Rule 31 (dispatch-policy.md:64) defines a delivered stop as a stop whose state is 'delivered' or 'handedOver'.

requirement: `previewPlan` returns a dry-run result without invoking storage.
`redactAccessLog` removes token and secret fields while preserving other fields.
`orderedDestinationGroups` returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.
finding: groupByDestination returns a Map (line 9). orderedDestinationGroups passes it to orderManifestGroups (line 42), which spreads it into [key, group] entry arrays and reads .destination from those arrays (line 11), getting undefined. The comparator then returns 0 and the groups keep insertion order; a direct check with destinations 'b' then 'a' returned ['B', 'A'].

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md`, `routeDistance` rejects when no road connects two consecutive points.
`savePlan` validates a plan before the first persistent write.
`computeBackoff` doubles from 250 milliseconds and caps the result at 2000 milliseconds.
`retryTransient` permits retries only for errors explicitly marked transient.
Under `docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md`, `locateStops` leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.
finding: locateStops removes only results that are exactly undefined (line 34). docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md:3 defines lookup only for a known address and does not state what an unknown address produces. If unknown lookups reject, Promise.all rejects instead of leaving out the stop, and a null result would be kept, so the adapter contract for unknown addresses is needed to decide the outcome.

requirement: `retainScheduleOffset` preserves the supplied offset exactly.
`runEligibleStops` skips cancelled stops while retaining the other stop order.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `withinVehicleCapacity` accepts a total equal to the configured limit.
finding: withinVehicleCapacity returns remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0 (line 3). When the weight equals the limit, the remaining capacity is 0 and the > 0 test refuses the total. A direct check of canAssignAllPackages (line 14) with one 10000 g package and a 10 kg limit returned false.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` treats an actor holding `routes:admin` as owning every depot.
finding: canPlanRoute checks routes:admin against actor.scopes (line 3) rather than held scopes, and held scopes include the scopes of active claims (rule 4, dispatch-policy.md:10). An actor whose routes:admin comes from an active claim is refused for a depot it does not own; a direct check returned false.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `canPlanRoute` refuses every suspended actor.
finding: For a suspended actor, effectiveScopes (line 5) drops the actor's own scopes but still adds scopes from active claims, so a suspended actor with an active routes:plan claim on its own depot is allowed; a direct check returned true. Rule 5 (dispatch-policy.md:11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes, and it is the later rule in the same section, so it overrides rule 4.

requirement: `selectActiveClaims` excludes claims before their start and at or after expiry.
`checksumPlan` hashes the bytes returned by the plan serializer.
Connect dispatch manifest publication through the public dispatch entry.
`safeAnnouncement` omits a top-level credential from the announcement payload.
`encodeUtf8` encodes publication bytes as UTF-8.
`manifestEntryIsValid` rejects blank package IDs.
Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishWithAnnouncement` removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.
finding: handleAnnouncementFailure gets the stored manifest through store.get (manifest.mjs:32), which resolves to a new copy (storage-contract.md:6), and passes that copy to store.remove. store.remove removes a stored manifest only when given that exact stored object (storage-contract.md:7), so the copy removes nothing and the stored manifest stays after a failed announcement.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `redactManifestEvent` removes every credential nested below an `auth` field.
finding: stripCredentials (line 14) recurses only into values whose constructor is Object, so an array nested below auth is returned unchanged and a credential inside it is kept; a direct check with auth.items[0].token returned 't'. Rule 24 (dispatch-policy.md:48) requires credential removal at every depth of the redacted value.

requirement: Given a positive integer maximum, `chunkManifest` limits every non-empty chunk to that configured maximum.
Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishWithAnnouncement` waits for the exact manifest to be durably stored before sending its announcement.
`serializeManifestRecords` emits NDJSON with one LF after every record, including the last.
`orderManifestGroups` orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `manifestRecipients` lists the contact phone of every manifest entry that has a `phone`.
`publicationResult` returns structured success and failure variants.
`normalizedPlanKey` trims and uppercases the route-key storage segment.
`buildManifest` copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.
finding: buildManifest spreads each record (line 26), but labelDriver (line 34) calls Object.assign on the driver object that the copied record still shares with the supplied record. The supplied record's driver label is changed; a direct check changed ' a ' to 'a'.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `publishWithRetry` stops after the allowed number of publication attempts.
`publishManifest` stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.
finding: Line 5 maps each entry to an async function, so checks holds Promise objects. A Promise is truthy, so checks.every(Boolean) on line 6 is always true and invalid entries are stored. A direct check with a blank packageId returned ok true and called store.put once.

requirement: `successTelemetry` records the success event, manifest ID, and timestamp.
`groupByDestination` groups records using normalized destination keys.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `departureMinute` is a stop's `arrivalMinute` plus its service time.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, `publishWithRetry` retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.
finding: asPublicationError (line 19) marks a failure transient when it has a finite retryAfter, even when error.transient is false. Rule 27 (dispatch-policy.md:54) says a failure marked transient: false is never transient, and it overrides rule 26 for that failure. Such a failure is therefore retried, because retryPublication (retry.mjs:14) continues when retryTransient returns true.

requirement: `preserveManifestDriver` trims driver labels without changing letter case.
`coalescePackages` removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.
finding: Line 37 filters normalized IDs against seen, but line 38 adds the raw group.packageIds values to seen. A package ID with surrounding spaces is therefore stored in its raw form, and a later trimmed duplicate is not removed. A direct check with [' P1'] followed by ['P1'] kept 'P1' in both groups.

requirement: Stop ordering uses descending priority followed by ascending sequence.
Publication audit records include action, actor, and timestamp.
Window membership includes both the declared start and end hour.
Schedule offsets pass through without coercion.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.
finding: routeDuration adds stop.serviceMinutes (queue.mjs:32) but not the 5 parking minutes that rule 32 (dispatch-policy.md:65) includes in a stop's service time. A stop with serviceMinutes 10 and travelMinutes 0 adds 10 minutes instead of 15.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.
finding: stripCredentials (line 14) recurses only into values whose constructor is Object, so an array nested below auth is returned unchanged and a credential inside it is kept; a direct check with auth.items[0].token returned 't'. Rule 24 (dispatch-policy.md:48) requires credential removal at every depth of the redacted value.

requirement: Empty manifests use an empty entries array and a generated marker.
Publication failure telemetry includes the manifest ID, error, and timestamp.
Driver labels are trimmed without changing their letter case.
`savePlan` completes validation before its first write.
Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.
finding: handleAnnouncementFailure gets the stored manifest through store.get (manifest.mjs:32), which resolves to a new copy (storage-contract.md:6), and passes that copy to store.remove. store.remove removes a stored manifest only when given that exact stored object (storage-contract.md:7), so the copy removes nothing and the manifest written earlier in the operation stays stored after the announcement fails.

requirement: Package IDs are trimmed, deduplicated, and sorted lexically.
Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.
finding: Line 37 filters normalized IDs against seen, but line 38 adds the raw group.packageIds values to seen. A package ID with surrounding spaces is therefore stored in its raw form, and a later trimmed duplicate across destination groups is not removed. A direct check with [' P1'] followed by ['P1'] kept 'P1' in both groups.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.
finding: The catch block calls store.discardTemporary() (storage.mjs:9) after renameTemporary rejects. Under storage-contract.md:11 the temporary bytes are locked after a rejected rename, and storage-contract.md:13 says discardTemporary only closes the write and keeps locked bytes. Only store.removeTemporary (storage-contract.md:14) deletes locked bytes, so the temporary bytes stay in place after the failure.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, `publishManifest` returns, in a success result, the manifest object that `store.put` durably stored.
Eligible-stop execution excludes cancelled stops.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.
finding: canAssignAllPackages delegates to withinVehicleCapacity (line 3), which returns remainingVehicleCapacity(limit * 1000, weight) > 0. A total equal to the limit leaves 0 remaining capacity, so it is refused; a direct check with one 10000 g package and a 10 kg limit returned false.

requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.
finding: index.mjs does not re-export executor.mjs or runtime.mjs, so the execution operations defined in executor.mjs (executeAuthorizedPlan, executeDryRun, runEligibleStops and pendingStops) are not exported by the public dispatch entry.

requirement: Publication success telemetry includes the manifest ID and timestamp.
Plan previews return without touching persistent storage.
Appending a stable stop returns a new list.
Dispatch backoff is capped at 2000 milliseconds.
Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.
finding: withSortedKeys (line 1) wraps only the top-level object, so JSON.stringify keeps the insertion order of nested objects and serializePlan (line 3) produces different text for plans that differ only in nested key order. A direct check of checksumPlan on {a:{x:1,y:2}} and {a:{y:2,x:1}} produced different digests.

requirement: Transient retry classification requires an explicit true marker.
Depot ownership requires equal actor and route depot identifiers.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.
finding: urgent uses priorityOf (default 5 for non-finite priority, line 4) while remaining uses the raw test !(stop.priority > 5) (line 23). A stop with priority Infinity or a numeric string such as '9' is absent from both partitions; a direct check with priority Infinity returned empty urgent and remaining lists. Rules 15 and 16 (dispatch-policy.md:30-31) define the priority used for urgency.

requirement: Destination keys are normalized with NFKC, trimmed, and uppercased.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.
finding: nextDispatchTime tests the blackout with candidate.getHours() (schedule.mjs:15), which reads the local hour, while rule 10 (dispatch-policy.md:22) requires UTC hours and rules 12 and 13 (dispatch-policy.md:24-25) apply to those hours. The blackout move therefore depends on the machine time zone. The later-bound selection on line 14 is correct.

requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated hands its emitter callback to savePlan as onStored, and savePlan passes it to store.write as onCommit (storage.mjs:4). docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md does not define store.write or when onCommit runs relative to a durable write, so whether plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds cannot be established from the staged bytes and the governing contracts.

requirement: Access-log redaction removes both token and secret fields.
Under `docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md`, atomic plan writes rename the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
`toStableJson` uses two-space indentation and one terminal LF.
`orderManifestGroups` orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Manifest NDJSON ends every record, including the final record, with LF.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.
finding: compareStops uses (left.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), which replaces only null or undefined. A sequence that is not finite, such as the string 'n/a', yields NaN in the subtraction, and NaN || ... leaves the comparator result as NaN, which sort treats as equal. Such stops are not placed after stops of equal priority that have a finite sequence, as rule 18 (dispatch-policy.md:33) requires.

requirement: Destination grouping uses normalized keys and copied records.
Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.
finding: authorizeRouteBatch returns firstRejected <= 0 (line 9). When the first route (index 0) fails depot ownership, firstRejected is 0 and the batch is accepted; a direct check with routes [Y, X] for an actor on depot X returned true.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
finding: weighPackages stores the result of scale.read unchanged. docs/dispatch/adapter-contracts.md:8 gives the scale.read result as a measured weight without a unit, while rule 28 (dispatch-policy.md:58) requires grams. The unit of the scale adapter is not established by the staged bytes or the governing contracts, so the unit recorded cannot be verified.

requirement: Blackout intervals include the start and exclude the end.
Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: Line 4 evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) as an argument before unlessForbidden checks canPlanRoute, so dispatch runs before the authorization decision. A direct check with an unauthorized actor invoked dispatch once.

requirement: Successful publication results and failed publication results use distinct structured variants.
Blank package IDs make a manifest entry invalid.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a driver's workload counts exactly the stops whose assigned driver is that driver.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.
finding: Line 4 relies on Number(value) coercion, so the empty string (Number('') is 0) and '1e0' are accepted; direct checks returned ok true for both. Rule 22 (dispatch-policy.md:43) accepts text retry counts only when they are one or more base-10 digits.

requirement: Serialized plan parsing returns structured success or failure.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the delivered-stop count counts exactly the delivered stops.
The ordinary stop-ordering operation sorts a copy of its input.
Stops at the vehicle weight limit remain in the accepted partition.
Given a positive integer maximum, manifest chunks never exceed that configured size.
`normalizeRouteKey` applies NFKC before trimming and uppercasing.
Normalized plan storage keys trim and uppercase route keys.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, measured vehicle limits use the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.
finding: asPublicationError (line 19) marks a failure transient when it has a finite retryAfter, even when error.transient is false. Rule 27 (dispatch-policy.md:54) says a failure marked transient: false is never transient, so a failure that the classification rules do not make transient is still retried.

requirement: UTF-8 encoding uses the explicit `utf8` encoding name.
Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.
finding: For a suspended actor, effectiveScopes (line 5) drops the actor's own scopes but still adds scopes from active claims, so a suspended actor with an active routes:plan claim on its own depot can plan the route; a direct check returned true. Rule 5 (dispatch-policy.md:11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.
finding: sendDeliveryNotices passes entry.phone unchanged to sms.send (publisher.mjs:31), while rule 33 (dispatch-policy.md:66) defines the contact phone with spaces and hyphens removed. manifestRecipients (manifest.mjs:44) applies that normalization, but the delivery path does not. Entries without a phone are also sent to with an undefined recipient.

requirement: Under `docs/dispatch/dispatch-policy.md`, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides `retryAfter`.
finding: nextRetryDelay (retry.mjs:24) tests retryAfter for truthiness, so a finite numeric retryAfter of 0 is ignored and computeBackoff applies instead of the server delay; a direct check of nextRetryDelay(1, 0) returned 500 instead of 0. Rules 6 and 7 (dispatch-policy.md:15-16) require a finite numeric retryAfter to replace the computed backoff.
